title: Functions Part 1 Challenge - The Karel Robot
summary: Practises writing and calling your own functions in the Stanford Karel robot simulator: reach the far corner of a 5x5 world, draw a diagonal line of beepers using a reusable function, and optionally build a chessboard pattern.

concepts.heading: The Karel environment
points: Karel is a simple robot in an online editor; set the world size to 5 x 5 for a smaller grid.
Code placed in function main() runs when Run is pressed; reset returns Karel to the start between runs.
Built-in commands: move() steps one square forward in the facing direction, turnLeft() rotates 90 degrees left, putBeeper() drops a marker on the square, pickBeeper() removes one.
Each command is a function call, so it needs brackets and a semicolon.
You can define extra functions outside main and call them from main; the spelling at the call must match the declaration exactly.
(Extra) If no turnRight() is available in your Karel editor, define one as three turnLeft() calls.

concepts.heading: Using functions to avoid repetition
points: A repeated group of commands (four move() calls in a row) can be extracted into a named function such as moveFourTimes(), then called in several places.
Benefits: shorter code, and bugs are easier to localise because a wrong step count lives in one function.
Example demo function goInCircle() combines move() and turnLeft() calls and is called from main; calling it twice completes a full loop.

code_examples.caption: Challenge 1: bottom-left to top-right corner using a helper
Challenge 2: diagonal of five beepers with a repeated unit

task.name: Karel challenges
task.starting_point: Karel editor via the link in the lesson resources, world set to 5 x 5, main() emptied.
task.goal: Three tasks of increasing difficulty using functions.
steps: Challenge 1: write code moving Karel from the bottom-left to the top-right corner. Any route counts; one route is four moves, turn left, four moves.
Refactor the repeated move() calls into moveFourTimes() and call it twice.

Challenge 2: make Karel place a diagonal of five beepers from bottom-left to top-right, with as little repeated code as possible: put the repeating unit (move, turnLeft, move, putBeeper, turn right) into a named function and call it four times after the first putBeeper().
Optional challenge 3: create a chessboard pattern of alternating beeper squares (solution is in the lesson resources).
task.expected_result: Karel ends in the top-right corner; a diagonal line of five beepers; optionally an alternating chessboard of beepers.

pitfalls: Misspelling a function name between its declaration and call.
Forgetting that Karel keeps facing the new direction after turnLeft(), so the order of moves matters.
Forgetting the first putBeeper() before the repeated unit, giving only four beepers.
Reference repo has no Karel code for this lesson; the chess-board solution is given in the next article lecture.

playground.coverage: The playground lesson covers define/call with a milk robot, but has no Karel task.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a mini Karel-style grid widget (canvas or divs) with move(), turnLeft(), putBeeper() exposed so learners can run the corner-to-corner and diagonal challenges in the page.
Add tasks: corner-to-corner, refactor to moveFourTimes, diagonal of beepers, chessboard.
Include a link to the Stanford Karel editor as an alternative.
